fields.features_heading: What a Restaurant Page Needs to Work
fields.features_subheading: Each part below decides whether a request reaches the person who can say yes, and Emergent changes any of them by prompt.
fields.feature_1:
The menu for this offer only

Show the dishes and prices that belong to the offer, such as the five courses of a tasting dinner. Link to the full menu once, at the bottom, for the guest who asks for it.
fields.feature_2:
A number a thumb can reach

Put the phone number in a tap-to-call button near the top, with the street address and a directions link under it. A guest choosing a place for dinner tonight calls first.
fields.feature_3:
A row for every request

Each request lands in a database you own with the guest's name, the date, the time, and the party size. A status column lets the manager mark each row Confirmed or Declined.
fields.feature_4:
An alert to whoever confirms

Send each request by email or to a Slack channel the front of house reads. The alert carries the guest's name, number, and party size, so the reply can start right away.
fields.feature_5:
The notice the kitchen needs

Print how far ahead a request has to arrive, such as 48 hours for a catering order. A guest who reads the cutoff before picking a date sends a request the kitchen can fill.
fields.feature_6:
A web address guests know

Publish the page on the domain already printed on your menus, or on a subdomain of it for events and catering. Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits.

fields.hero_prompt: Build a restaurant landing page that saves every signup to a database I own.

faq_plan.q: What is a restaurant landing page?
How do I create a restaurant landing page?

plan.angle: A restaurant site already carries the menu, the hours and the address; a restaurant landing page does one job that the site does badly, such as a large-party request, a catering quote, a ticketed holiday dinner or a list for a new location. This page shows four of those pages with the form, the rule behind it and the row each request leaves in a database the owner keeps, then gives seven build steps an owner or general manager can follow. It makes no health-code, liquor, payment or delivery-platform claims, and the wedding sibling stays out of the headings.
tab_stories: Peppervine Bistro asks for party size first; a request for 8 or more guests emails events manager Rosalind Haddix instead of offering a table time, and of 64 requests this week 9 went to her and 55 picked a time.

Stonewick Smokehouse takes catering requests with the date, the guest count and pickup or delivery; every order for 50 or more guests goes to catering lead Teo Beaty, and this month he got 12 of 31 requests while 19 went to the kitchen.
Lark Hollow Tavern sells 40 seats for a $95 New Year's Eve tasting menu; once 40 seats are reserved the form takes waitlist names instead, and 14 people have joined the waitlist.

Sartino's Pizzeria is opening a second location in Westvale and asks each signup which location they would visit; of 212 signups, 138 picked Westvale and get the opening-night invite, and 74 picked Downtown.
